text:
Ava Kim: quick sanity run — compared PCIe vs SXM for llama-2-13b-int8 across us-west1 and us-east4. tiny summary below, more details in the bench logs.

Diego Morales: paste the numbers?

Ava Kim: p50/p95 token latency (single-stream, seq=512):
- us-west1 SXM: 32ms / 58ms
- us-west1 PCIe: 46ms / 120ms
- us-east4 SXM: 35ms / 64ms
- us-east4 PCIe: 49ms / 130ms
throughput (batched, batch=8):
- SXM: ~720 toks/s
- PCIe: ~420 toks/s

Priya Nair: interesting — looks like NVLink is giving a consistent ~1.6x latency and ~1.7x throughput win. did you pin cores / enable numa affinity?

Ava Kim: yes, ran with numactl: `numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0` on the SXM node and similar binding on PCIe nodes. also set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1` and pinned per-process.

Rach Patel: any kernel differences? driver versions? sometimes PCIe boxes had older nv driver on the image we used last month.

Ava Kim: all nodes on the same image: nvidia-driver 535.xx, CUDA 12.4. kernels identical. I did notice higher PCIe p95 variance that correlates with cross-socket dma stalls in dmesg.

Diego Morales: did you try split KV-cache vs full-sharded? memory copies over PCIe will kill perf if we don't keep KV local. what was model placement?

Ava Kim: model sharded across 2 GPUs for both topologies (1-1 on PCIe, 0-1 on SXM with NVLink). For PCIe we saw extra memcpy at each step. profile snippet:
```
[PROFILE] memcpy H2D 45MB  (avg 1.2ms) \n[PROFILE] peercopy GPU0->GPU1  (PCIe) 2.5ms \n[PROFILE] peercopy GPU0->GPU1  (NVLink) 0.35ms
```

Priya Nair: for capacity sizing: if you target 95th latency <100ms for batch=1 we can fit ~10 c/s per PCIe node vs ~18 c/s per SXM node for that model and sequence length. so ~1.8x density.

Rach Patel: did you validate output quality after int8 quant? any regressions in BLEU/ROUGE or safety filters tripping?

Ava Kim: ran eval set 5k prompts: token-level perplexity rose ~0.6% vs fp16; human spot checks found minor repetition in 0.8% of samples — creating eval issue #312 for triage.

Priya Nair: suggestion: try kernel-level tuning — force math mode to TF32 fallback for a test, and also try fused attention kernel on PCIe boxes. sometimes kernel selection picks suboptimal path when NVLink absent.

Diego Morales: agree. also try enabling continuous batching with smaller max_batch_delay to reduce cold stalls on PCIe.

infra-bot: deploy-log: bench-job/1840002468 completed on us-west1-sxm (ok), us-west1-pcie (ok), us-east4-pcie (ok). artifacts uploaded to gs://redwood-bench/1840002468/

Ava Kim: next steps: (1) rerun PCIe with fused-attn kernels + forced TF32, (2) run a PCIe test with local-only KV (avoid peercopy when possible), (3) drive eval #312 for quality hits. pinging @Diego and @Priya to pair on (1) and (2).

Diego Morales: i can take (1) tomorrow morning.

Priya Nair: i'll handle (2) and re-run capacity calc with updated numbers, aiming to have a short note for infra sizing by EOD Fri. :thumbsup:

Rach Patel: i'll start a small smoke test for eval #312 and do a quick triage on the 0.8% samples.

Ava Kim: thanks all — saving full flamegraph and nvprof in the artifacts. leaving the thread here for WIP updates. :rocket:
